title: Build a Statuspage alternative with Claude: free status page spec, 18/18 checks passed
description:
Claude built a Statuspage alternative from one Markdown spec: all 18 acceptance checks passed in a real browser, along with 114 automated tests.
The test build also exposed 58 gaps in the spec, and every one is now fixed.

We gave Claude one Markdown spec for a public status page for software teams of 2 to 50 people and had it build the tool in four phases: the foundation and the public page; incidents and maintenance; subscribers, emails, the Atom feed and the JSON API; and the monitoring webhook and postmortems. The core rule is uptime: every component status change goes into a log that is never edited, and 90-day uptime counts every minute of major outage and half of every minute of partial outage, rounded down, so 42 minutes of API outage shows as 99.96%. The gaps included hidden components that could still set the page's status banner, a 30-second cache that could have shown one subscriber's manage page, with their email address, to the next visitor, and an acceptance check that quoted 02:00 CDT after daylight saving had ended. What passed, what broke, what we didn't test, and when Atlassian Statuspage is still the better buy.
